THE_FINDING_OF_THIS_SESSION: The working-directory probe created the failure it reported, and only the coordinator's independent re-run could see it. The build agent reported 0 non-zero exits in 44 runs of probe_working_directories.py. The coordinator's run found 1: validate_examples.py from the repository root, exit 1. Because the release gate runs every validation/*.py, that single exit would have BLOCKED P081. Cause: validate_examples.py unlinks each shared screenshots/*.png and regenerates it, then asserts the figure exists and exceeds 10,000 bytes; the probe dispatched all 44 script-directory pairs into a two-worker pool, so two copies of that one script could overlap and one would delete a figure the other was about to measure.
WHY_THAT_FINDING_IS_NOT_JUST_A_BUG: It is the sixth occurrence in this mission of the class the build guide names - a check whose own execution can create the condition it tests is not a check - and the SECOND in which the HARNESS rather than the script is the polluter, after release-gate check 2 writing .ruff_cache before check 6 reads the tree, which cost P084 a night. It is also a case where the build guide's existing remedies would all have passed it: the script exits 0 run alone from the directory the probe blames, and two copies started by hand did not collide. The few-millisecond window between one copy's unlink and the other's stat needs the probe's own four-runs-over-two-workers dispatch to be hit at all, at roughly 1 in 44. An intermittent self-inflicted failure is invisible to any number of agreeing serial verifications.
probe_fixed_at_cause_and_verified_twice: Each script's four directory runs are now grouped onto one worker and executed serially, while different scripts still run two at a time, so the same 44 runs spread over the same two workers and the wall-clock cost is unchanged (436.1 s before, 449.4 s and 442.6 s after; the difference is noise on two cores). Separately the probe reported only the failing script's stderr, and these scripts report failed checks on stdout and exit 1 with an empty stderr, so the one real failure it has ever caught printed NO detail at all; it now falls back to stdout. Per the build guide the fixed probe was run TWICE from a clean tree: 0 of 44 and 0 of 14 both times, with byte-identical per-directory status tables. One clean run would have been weak evidence against a 1-in-44 intermittent failure.
P084_NARROWING_CONFIRMED_EMPIRICALLY: The gate left 32 cache artifacts in P081's tree - .ruff_cache plus 31 __pycache__ entries and .pyc files - which is EXACTLY the condition that made P084 ungateable on 2026-11-01.
